The test image shows a corn field with clear variation in plant heights — several plants appear noticeably stunted compared to their neighbors, with some yellowing/pale coloration on the shorter plants. No visible lesions, rust pustules, or ear symptoms.

Key features: patchy stunting across the field, reduced plant height, some chlorosis on affected plants.

This pattern strongly suggests a systemic disease. Top candidates: Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus, Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus.

Let me view one reference image for Corn Stunt Spiroplasma to confirm.

The reference image for Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma shows close-up purple/black ear symptoms, which doesn't match my test image well. The test image is a field-level view showing patchy stunting — several plants are noticeably shorter than neighbors, with some yellowing, on red/clay soil (consistent with African context).

The patchy stunting across the field with otherwise green plants is the defining visual. Corn Stunt Spiroplasma causes exactly this: infected plants are severely stunted while adjacent plants remain normal height. The reference image I saw was a close-up showing later-stage symptoms, but the field-level stunting pattern is the hallmark of this disease.
